title: Calculate the Height of a Binary Tree
real_world_story: A compression system stores encoded data using a binary tree. The system needs to determine how many levels the tree contains to understand the structure and depth of the encoded representation.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A binary tree stored using node relationships
real_world_connection.target_represents: The number of levels in the binary tree
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Recursively determining the maximum depth of the left and right subtrees

problem_statement: Given a binary tree represented using an array in level-order where -1 represents a missing node, find the height of the binary tree. The height is defined as the number of nodes on the longest path from the root to a leaf.
task: Build the binary tree from the given level-order representation and return its height.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of positions in the level-order representation. The second line contains N space-separated integers. A value of -1 represents a missing node.
output_format: Print the height of the binary tree. If the tree is empty, print 0.
constraints: The first position represents the root

examples.explanation: The longest root-to-leaf path contains three nodes: 1 → 2 → 4.
The root has two children, so the tree contains two levels.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Trees
expected_algorithm.reason: The height of a binary tree can be determined by recursively finding the maximum height of its left and right subtrees.

hint: Build the binary tree from the level-order representation.
The height of an empty tree is 0.
For every node, find the height of its left and right subtrees.
Return one plus the larger subtree height.
real_world_takeaway: Understanding binary-tree structure helps compression systems organize hierarchical encoded data and analyze the depth of the resulting representation.
